note: Independent rejudgment 2026-11-15 of the unchanged requirement and all ten tagged functions after four received-identifier fixture topology additions and the whole-set RIB consumer topology repair. RFC 4271 Section 9.1.2.2 states: 'The criteria MUST be applied in the order specified.' The full criteria (a)-(g), including whole-set elimination and MED comparability only within the neighboring AS, were read. Section 9.1.2 first excludes an unresolvable NEXT_HOP. Each structured and production-JSON identifier test now supplies only an independent connected 10.0.0.1/32 route, with real prospective Loc-RIB resolution and cost zero. UPDATE bytes, two candidates, peer addresses and BGP Identifiers are unchanged. The positive pair makes step f choose the higher-address peer with the lower BGP Identifier; the negative pair ties identifiers and requires step g to choose the lower peer address. These tests exercise metadata extraction through actual received events and assert exact comparison steps and winners. The topology adds no admission bypass and leaves unknown-next-hop controls unchanged. The unchanged adjacent-criteria test conflicts each earlier criterion with the next in both argument orders. The unchanged whole-set MED candidate tests cover all six permutations, require C to lose to A at MED before B beats A at Router ID, and forbid an earlier-criteria loser from eliminating C at MED. FullTiebreak and same-neighbor MED remain supplementary; the latter also prevents a different neighboring AS from winning through its lower MED. The selection producer removes earlier-criteria losers before grouping same-neighbor MED survivors and comparing later criteria. TestRFC4271WholeSetMEDRIBBestChange now supplies only independent connected routes to its unchanged next hops 192.0.2.3, 192.0.2.2 and 192.0.2.1. Its six permutations still exercise actual received attributes, exact Loc-RIB B-to-C-to-B selection as non-best MED witness A leaves and returns, exact replacement events and no spurious unchanged publication. Main's b6e1a9ef baseline passed this consumer with race (1.650s); the earlier 4d7e8db1 selected repaired RIB roots and peer regression passed with race and no skips. I inspected all five new RFC4271 normal-return semantic proof logs and their current native records. In d5b651a5 and 28d0bd7d, reversing compareAfterMED's Router ID comparison first passed the named structured or JSON baseline, then failed its exact winner assertion: expected 192.0.2.2, actual 192.0.2.1. In 147c6181 and c7ad240b, reversing the peer-address comparison first passed each equal-Identifier baseline, then failed its exact winner assertion: expected 192.0.2.1, actual 192.0.2.2. In 3c3ec480, replacing retainLowestMED's selected survivor count with the full eligible count first passed the whole-set RIB consumer baseline, then failed the first Loc-RIB winner assertion: expected B through 192.0.2.2, actual A through 192.0.2.1. The observed winner was A, not the proposal's predicted C; the actual incorrect winner is the evidence. These five native mutant records bind the changed unit bodies and each precise claim. They show ordinary assertion failures, not panics, skips or build failures, and do not extend proof to other breaks.
